answer: In a staked agent economy each actor locks collateral before bidding, and that bond is slashed when audits catch it faking identities. A Sybil farmer spinning up a thousand clones at a wharf must fund a thousand separate bonds, so attack cost scales with every fake persona instead of near zero. Honest operators counterfeit nothing, so their capital stays parked and accrues reputation, while the impostor's stake burns at the first double-vote. A bonded ledger makes duplication expensive: trust grows like a willow, and anyone climbing onto a rival's ledge forfeits the deposit behind it.
